laws.title: Nigerian Greetings — Vary by Region and Religion
laws.subtitle: Yoruba, Hausa and Igbo cultures have distinct customs
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria is incredibly diverse — over 250 ethnic groups with distinct customs. Generally: always greet elders first and show respect. In the north (predominantly Muslim): Salami alaikum greeting, gender separation norms. In the south (Yoruba culture): prostrating for men, kneeling for women when greeting elders is traditional. Handshakes (sometimes snapping fingers together) are common. Accepting food or drink is polite.
laws.penalty: Not legal — disrespecting elders or religious customs causes significant social offence.
exceptions: Lagos is very cosmopolitan and international
International business settings follow global norms

quiz.q: What traditional greeting gesture do Yoruba men perform when greeting elders?
quiz.explanation: In Yoruba culture, men traditionally prostrate (lie flat) briefly when greeting elders as a sign of deep respect.

laws.title: LGBTQ+ Laws — Criminal; Same-Sex Marriage Prohibition Act 2014
laws.subtitle: SSMPA 2014 — 14 years imprisonment; mob violence documented
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria's Same Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act 2014 (SSMPA) criminalises same-sex marriage, civil unions, and public displays of same-sex affection with up to 14 years imprisonment. In northern Nigeria's Sharia states, the death penalty applies. LGBTQ+ organisations are also banned. Violence against LGBTQ+ people is common and police are known to participate or enable it. This is one of the world's most dangerous countries for LGBTQ+ people.
laws.penalty: Same-sex marriage/unions: 14 years. Public same-sex affection: 10 years. Northern Sharia law: death penalty. Belonging to LGBTQ+ groups: 10 years.
exceptions: No legal exceptions — extremely dangerous for LGBTQ+ travellers

quiz.q: What is the maximum penalty for same-sex marriage in Nigeria under the SSMPA 2014?
quiz.explanation: Nigeria's SSMPA 2014 carries 14 years imprisonment for same-sex marriage — with the death penalty applying in some northern Sharia-law states.

laws.title: Advance Fee Fraud (419) — Victim Caution
laws.subtitle: Economic and Financial Crimes Commission — EFCC active
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria is internationally associated with '419 scams' (advance fee fraud, named after §419 of the Nigerian Penal Code). The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) actively prosecutes fraud. However, foreign victims who travel to Nigeria in relation to a scam are at risk of being further victimised, robbed, or kidnapped. The EFCC website has resources for reporting fraud. If approached online by someone claiming to be Nigerian offering business or romance: be very sceptical.
laws.penalty: Perpetrators of 419 fraud: up to 5 years imprisonment + fine. Victims who co-operate in their own defrauding have no legal protection.
exceptions: Legitimate Nigerian business is extensive and growing
Lagos and Abuja have large legitimate business communities
laws.sourceLabel: Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) — Nigeria

quiz.q: What is Nigeria's '419 scam' named after?
options: Section 419 of the Nigerian Penal Code
quiz.explanation: 419 scams are named after §419 of the Nigerian Penal Code — the section criminalising advance fee fraud, making 'Nigerian prince' scams one of the world's most notorious.

laws.title: Traffic Laws — Right-Side Driving; Strict Checkpoints
laws.subtitle: Federal Highway Authority — Right side; mobile phone ban
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria drives on the right side of the road. The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) operates extensive checkpoints nationwide. Mobile phone use while driving is prohibited and strictly enforced. Drink driving limit: 0.05g/100ml BAC (strictly enforced before major holidays). Motorcycles (okadas) are banned in many parts of Lagos, Abuja, and other major cities. Vehicle roadworthiness checks are required. On long-distance routes, travel at night is strongly discouraged due to armed robbery.
laws.penalty: Mobile phone while driving: NGN 5,000 fine. Drink driving: criminal charge. Riding banned okada: confiscation + fine.
exceptions: Licensed inter-state transport carriers
Emergency vehicles

quiz.q: Which side of the road does Nigeria drive on?
quiz.explanation: Nigeria drives on the right side of the road — a legacy of its colonial history and consistent with most of continental Africa and the rest of the world.

laws.title: Cybercrime Act 2015 — Social Media and Online Fraud
laws.subtitle: Cybercrimes (Prohibition, Prevention etc) Act 2015
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria's Cybercrimes Act 2015 is wide-ranging and includes provisions against online fraud, cyberstalking, and 'cybersquatting'. Critically, Section 24 criminalises sending electronic messages that are 'grossly offensive, pornographic or of an indecent, obscene or menacing character' or any material that provokes others. This provision has been used to prosecute government critics and journalists. Social media activity, satirical posts, and critical commentary about public officials have led to arrests under this section. Nigeria also has major online fraud issues ('Yahoo boys') and law enforcement has broad powers to investigate.
laws.penalty: Section 24 (offensive online posts): up to 3 years imprisonment + fine. Online fraud: 3–7 years. Cyberstalking: up to 10 years.
exceptions: Journalism and public interest expression — but Section 24 has a broad interpretation
Academic cybersecurity research with proper notification

quiz.q: What has Nigeria's Section 24 of the Cybercrimes Act 2015 been used to prosecute?
options: Government critics and satirists on social media
quiz.explanation: Nigeria's Section 24 criminalises 'grossly offensive' online messages — and has been used to arrest government critics and journalists for social media commentary.

laws.title: Land Use Act 1978 — All Land in Nigeria Belongs to the Government
laws.subtitle: Land Use Act Cap L5 LFN 2004 — No freehold land ownership for individuals
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria's Land Use Act 1978 (consolidated as Cap L5, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria 2004) establishes one of the most unusual property regimes in the world: all land in each state of Nigeria is vested in the Governor of that state, who holds it in trust for the people. No individual or company owns land outright in the freehold sense. Instead, people hold a 'right of occupancy' — either a statutory right of occupancy (granted by the Governor) or a customary right of occupancy (for rural areas). This means that when Nigerians buy and sell 'land', they are actually transferring rights of occupancy, not freehold ownership. The Governor can revoke a right of occupancy for overriding public interest — for example, for government projects or public infrastructure — with compensation paid only for unexhausted improvements (e.g., buildings), not for the land itself. This creates significant barriers to using land as collateral for bank loans and is widely blamed for constraining Nigeria's mortgage market and property investment. Expats and foreign investors must be especially careful: foreign nationals cannot hold rights of occupancy directly; investment must go through a Nigerian-registered company.
laws.penalty: Occupying or using land without a valid right of occupancy: liable to prosecution. Fraudulent transfer of land rights: criminal fraud charges under the Criminal Code.
exceptions: Oil and gas companies operate under separate petroleum laws that override some Land Use Act provisions
Federal government land (used for federal infrastructure) is separately governed under federal legislation
laws.sourceLabel: Land Use Act Cap L5 — Laws of the Federation of Nigeria 2004

quiz.q: Under Nigeria's Land Use Act 1978, who legally owns all land in each Nigerian state?
options: The Governor of each state, held in trust for the people
quiz.explanation: Nigeria's Land Use Act 1978 vests all land in each state in the state Governor, held in trust for the people — no individual holds freehold ownership of land in Nigeria.

laws.title: Nigerian Land Use Act — All Land Belongs to the Government; No Freehold Ownership
laws.subtitle: Land Use Act 1978 — Citizens hold 'right of occupancy', not ownership
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria's Land Use Act 1978 (cap L5, LFN 2004) is a foundational but controversial law: it vests all land in each state in the Governor, held in trust for the people. Individuals and corporations do not own land outright — they hold a 'Certificate of Occupancy' (C of O) granting a right of use for up to 99 years. This means a Governor can revoke your right of occupancy for 'overriding public interest' with limited compensation. The Act has been criticised for discouraging long-term investment, complicating mortgages, and enabling government land grabs. Foreigners cannot hold a C of O directly — they must use a Nigerian incorporated company.
laws.penalty: Building without a C of O: fine + demolition order. Foreigners attempting to hold land directly (not through a company): legal nullity + forfeiture.
exceptions: Federal government land (acquired under Federal Land Use Act provisions)
Communities with established customary land tenure recognised by state legislation
laws.sourceLabel: Nigeria Office of the Surveyor General — Land Use Act

quiz.q: Under Nigeria's Land Use Act 1978, who holds the right to all land within each Nigerian state?
options: The State Governor in trust for the people
quiz.explanation: Nigeria's Land Use Act 1978 vests all land in each state in the State Governor, held in trust for the people — meaning no individual or corporation technically 'owns' land, only holds a right of occupancy.

laws.title: Nollywood and Film Regulations — Nigerian Film and Video Censors Board
laws.subtitle: NFVCB — All films must be classified; street photography in Lagos has sensitivities
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria's film industry (Nollywood) is the world's second-largest by volume — producing over 2,500 films per year. The Nigerian Film and Video Censors Board (NFVCB) classifies all films released in Nigeria — films with explicit sexual content, excessive violence, or content 'repugnant to good morals' are banned. Foreign films can be shown but must be registered with the NFVCB. Street photography in Lagos requires awareness: photographing police officers, military personnel, or government buildings without permission is technically prohibited. Lagos is also one of Africa's most creatively vibrant cities — the Lekki Arts and Crafts Market and Osogbo's Sacred Groves (UNESCO) have specific photography and conduct protocols.
laws.penalty: Distributing an unclassified film: NFVCB fine + seizure. Photographing police/military without permission: camera confiscation + possible detention.
exceptions: Accredited press with NUJ (Nigerian Union of Journalists) card
Accredited foreign press with State Security Service (SSS) clearance for sensitive sites
laws.sourceLabel: Nigerian Film and Video Censors Board

quiz.q: By volume of films produced annually, what rank does Nigeria's Nollywood hold globally?
quiz.explanation: Nollywood is the world's second-largest film industry by volume — producing over 2,500 films per year, behind India's Bollywood but ahead of Hollywood. It serves a pan-African and global diaspora audience.

laws.title: Same-Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act 2014 — Criminalization of LGBTQ+ Relationships
laws.subtitle: Nigeria criminalizes same-sex relationships; northern Sharia states impose death penalty
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria's Same-Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act 2014 bans same-sex marriage and civil unions, criminalizes 'gay clubs, societies and organizations,' and prohibits public displays of same-sex affection — with up to 14 years imprisonment in secular federal law. In 12 northern states operating under Sharia law (Zamfara, Kano, Sokoto, etc.), male homosexuality can be punished by death (stoning). The law is broadly worded to include 'gay clubs' and 'same-sex amorous relationships in public.' LGBTQ+ rights organizations cannot legally operate. Nigeria has the third-largest LGBTQ+ prison population in Africa. Despite official position, enforcement varies significantly by region and social context in cosmopolitan Lagos and Abuja.
laws.penalty: Secular federal law: up to 14 years imprisonment. Northern Sharia states (for men): up to death by stoning. Supporting LGBTQ+ organizations: up to 10 years imprisonment.
exceptions: No formal legal exceptions exist
Enforcement is selective and varies dramatically by region
Diplomatic compounds and international organizations operate with de facto tolerance
laws.sourceLabel: UNHCR Refworld — Nigeria Same-Sex Marriage Prohibition Act 2014

quiz.q: In Nigeria's 12 northern Sharia-law states, what is the potential penalty for male homosexuality?
quiz.explanation: In Nigeria's 12 northern states operating under Sharia law, male homosexuality can be punishable by death — typically specified as stoning. This is separate from the federal secular law which carries up to 14 years imprisonment.

laws.title: Niger Delta Oil Spills — Shell's $15 Billion Liability and Ogoni Land Pollution
laws.subtitle: Nigeria's Niger Delta has 50+ years of oil spills; Shell paid $15.5B settlement; cleanup ongoing
laws.fullDescription: The Niger Delta has experienced one of the world's most severe oil pollution crises: an estimated 9–13 million barrels spilled over 50 years — more than the 1989 Exxon Valdez and 2010 Deepwater Horizon combined. The Ogoni people — led by Ken Saro-Wiwa (executed 1995 by the Abacha government for activism) — documented Shell's role in environmental destruction. The UN Environment Programme (UNEP) 2011 assessment of Ogoniland found contamination that would require 25–30 years and $1 billion to clean up. A landmark 2021 UK Court of Appeal ruling allowed Nigerian communities to sue Shell in English courts. Shell agreed to pay $15.5 billion to sell its Nigerian onshore subsidiary SPDC in 2023, partially reflecting ongoing liability. Nigeria's Environmental Guidelines for the Petroleum Industry (2020) impose stronger standards on operators.
laws.penalty: Oil operators causing spills: fines up to ₦10 million (~$12,600) under NOSDRA 2006 (widely criticized as insufficient). Criminal negligence: prosecution under Federal Environmental Protection Agency Act.
exceptions: Spills from third-party sabotage (bunkering/theft) have limited operator liability under current law
Force majeure events with documented evidence
Pipelines damaged by natural disasters

quiz.q: Ken Saro-Wiwa was executed in 1995 by Nigeria's Abacha government for what reason?
options: Organizing an armed rebellion against the government
Activism documenting Shell's oil pollution damage to the Ogoni people
Smuggling oil and evading petroleum taxes
Organizing an illegal strike by oil workers
quiz.explanation: Ken Saro-Wiwa was a writer and environmental activist who led the Movement for the Survival of the Ogoni People (MOSOP), documenting Shell's catastrophic oil pollution damage to Ogoniland. He was executed by Nigeria's military government under General Abacha in 1995, along with eight other Ogoni activists, in a case that drew international condemnation.

laws.title: #EndSARS Protests & Lekki Massacre
laws.subtitle: 2020 nationwide protests against SARS police unit brutality
laws.fullDescription: In October 2020, Nigerians launched the #EndSARS movement demanding disbandment of the Special Anti-Robbery Squad (SARS), notorious for extortion, torture, and extrajudicial killings targeting young people. On October 20, 2020, security forces opened fire on peaceful protesters at Lekki Toll Gate in Lagos — the Lekki Massacre. The Lagos Judicial Panel of Inquiry (2021) confirmed soldiers shot at protesters. SARS was officially disbanded and replaced by SWAT, though human rights groups report continued abuses. The protests represented Nigeria's largest civil unrest in decades.
laws.penalty: Protest organizers faced arbitrary arrest and terrorism charges. Several protesters remain detained. Security forces involved in Lekki shooting face judicial inquiry but limited prosecutions occurred.
exceptions: Right to peaceful assembly guaranteed under 1999 Constitution Section 40
Judicial panels were established to review police brutality claims
Some victims received compensation from Lagos State government

quiz.q: What was the primary demand of Nigeria's #EndSARS movement in 2020?
options: Disbandment of the SARS police unit
quiz.explanation: #EndSARS protesters demanded the disbandment of the Special Anti-Robbery Squad (SARS), a police unit accused of widespread extortion, torture, and extrajudicial killings.

laws.title: Naira Redesign Crisis & Cash Shortage
laws.subtitle: CBN's currency redesign created Nigeria's worst cash shortage — ATMs empty for weeks
laws.fullDescription: In October 2022, Central Bank of Nigeria Governor Godwin Emefiele announced a surprise deadline to replace old naira notes, ostensibly to mop up cash hoarded by corrupt politicians ahead of February 2023 elections. The rollout was catastrophic: new notes were not printed in sufficient quantity, old notes were invalidated before replacements arrived, ATMs went empty for weeks, businesses couldn't make change, and violence erupted at bank branches. The Supreme Court ordered old notes to remain valid; President Buhari defied the ruling for days before backing down. Emefiele was arrested in June 2023 on fraud charges. The chaos contributed to social unrest and election grievances.
laws.penalty: Refusing to accept legal tender (old or new naira during the transition): criminal offence. Hoarding cash: CBN enforcement actions. Financial institutions that prioritized VIPs for new notes faced CBN sanctions.
exceptions: Supreme Court order extended the validity of old naira notes during the crisis
Rural communities far from banks received extended grace periods
Point-of-sale operators (mobile banking agents) were exempt from some cash restrictions
laws.sourceLabel: Central Bank of Nigeria — Naira Redesign

quiz.q: What was the stated reason for Nigeria's Central Bank redesigning naira notes in late 2022?
options: To modernize the currency's security features
To mop up cash hoarded by politicians ahead of elections
To prepare for a digital currency transition
quiz.explanation: CBN Governor Emefiele stated the naira redesign aimed to reduce cash hoarding by politicians and corrupt officials ahead of the February 2023 elections — but the rushed implementation caused Nigeria's worst cash shortage in decades.

laws.title: Tinubu's Fuel Subsidy Removal & Reform Shock
laws.subtitle: Nigeria's new president ended a $10 billion annual fuel subsidy in his inauguration speech
laws.fullDescription: President Bola Tinubu's first words after taking office on May 29, 2023 were 'Fuel subsidy is gone' — ending Nigeria's expensive petrol subsidy that had cost over $10 billion annually. The removal was economically necessary: Nigeria was spending more on subsidizing fuel for the wealthy (who own most cars) than on health and education combined. However, the immediate impact was devastating for the poor: petrol prices tripled overnight, transport costs surged, food inflation hit 35%+, and the naira lost 70% of its value. Tinubu simultaneously unified the exchange rate, ending multiple tiers that had enabled corruption. The reforms were praised by the IMF but deeply unpopular.
laws.penalty: Fuel smuggling (made more profitable by subsidy removal): 5 years imprisonment. Illegal fuel adulteration: PPPRA enforcement. Price gouging during subsidy removal: FCCPC penalties.
exceptions: Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) conversion programs for commercial vehicles received subsidies as an offset
Some states briefly subsidized public transport fares as a cushion
Agricultural fuel use received temporary relief through CBN-funded programs

quiz.q: When did President Tinubu announce the end of Nigeria's fuel subsidy?
options: In his first state of the nation address after 100 days
In his inauguration speech on his first day as president
In a televised address three months into his term
quiz.explanation: Tinubu announced 'Fuel subsidy is gone' in his inauguration speech on May 29, 2023 — his very first day as president — ending a subsidy that had cost Nigeria over $10 billion annually, though the immediate impact tripled petrol prices and drove food inflation to 35%+.

laws.title: #EndSARS: Abolition of Nigeria's Feared Police Unit
laws.subtitle: Mass protests forced Nigeria to disband the notorious SARS police unit — but a new unit and similar abuses quickly followed
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria's Special Anti-Robbery Squad (SARS) was established in 1992 to combat armed robbery and kidnapping. It became notorious for extortion, arbitrary arrest, torture, and killing of young Nigerians — particularly targeting men with laptops, dreadlocks, or tattoos as suspected fraudsters ('Yahoo boys'). The #EndSARS protests of October 2020 drew millions across Nigeria and globally. On October 20, 2020, security forces opened fire on peaceful protesters at the Lekki toll gate in Lagos, killing an unknown number (official investigations acknowledged 1 death; witnesses reported 12+). The government disbanded SARS — but quickly created replacement units accused of similar abuses.
laws.penalty: SARS personnel faced no significant criminal prosecution. Protesters were arrested under public order laws. The government established a judicial panel that found security forces used excessive force at Lekki
exceptions: Some states implemented SARS replacement units with new names but similar personnel and mandates
Compensation was awarded to some victims' families by judicial panels in individual states

quiz.q: What characteristics made young Nigerians targets for SARS police harassment before the unit was disbanded?
options: Having laptops, dreadlocks, or tattoos — which police associated with cybercrime
quiz.explanation: SARS officers targeted young Nigerians with laptops, dreadlocks, tattoos, or expensive phones — stereotyping them as 'Yahoo boys' (internet fraudsters) — and extorted money or arrested them based on appearance alone.

laws.title: Nigeria Ends Fuel Subsidy: Petrol Prices Triple Overnight
laws.subtitle: President Tinubu ended Nigeria's decades-long fuel subsidy on his first day in office — sending petrol prices up 300% and triggering economic chaos
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria spent $10+ billion annually subsidizing fuel — one of Africa's most expensive subsidy programs — keeping petrol prices among Africa's lowest despite being the continent's largest oil producer. On May 29, 2023 — his inauguration day — President Bola Tinubu announced 'subsidy is gone,' immediately ending 40 years of fuel subsidies. Petrol prices tripled overnight. Within months, Nigeria also unified its multiple exchange rates, causing the naira to lose 70% of its value. Inflation surged to 34%. Cost-of-living protests erupted. In August 2024, Nigeria experienced its worst cost-of-living protests in decades, with at least 22 people killed. The IMF praised the reforms as necessary long-term corrections; ordinary Nigerians bore the immediate pain.
laws.penalty: No penalties for the policy itself — these are economic reforms. Price gouging by fuel retailers during the transition: fines from NNPC and regulatory agencies
exceptions: Some targeted subsidy schemes for mass transit and compressed natural gas were proposed as replacements
Electricity subsidies were maintained separately

quiz.q: On what significant day did President Tinubu announce the end of Nigeria's fuel subsidy?
options: His first day as president — inauguration day
The day after his election victory was certified
quiz.explanation: Tinubu announced 'subsidy is gone' on May 29, 2023 — his very first day as president during his inauguration speech — immediately ending 40 years of fuel subsidies and causing petrol prices to triple overnight.

laws.title: Oil Theft (Bunkering) Law
laws.subtitle: Nigeria criminalizes crude oil theft — a billion-dollar illegal industry
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria's Petroleum Industry Act 2021 and the Miscellaneous Offences Act make oil theft (illegal bunkering — tapping into pipelines) a serious criminal offense punishable by up to 21 years imprisonment. Nigeria loses an estimated 400,000–600,000 barrels of oil per day to theft — worth billions of dollars annually — through a sophisticated network of illegal connections to export pipelines, artisanal refineries ('kpo-fire' bush refineries), and corrupted officials. The Niger Delta has seen widespread violence linked to oil industry activities since the 1990s. The Petroleum Industry Act also requires oil companies to develop host communities, addressing decades of environmental injustice.
laws.penalty: Up to 21 years imprisonment for illegal bunkering; fines; vessel confiscation; operators of illegal refineries face the same penalties
exceptions: Licensed oil lifting by authorized companies is legal
Community pipeline surveillance contracts are permitted under the Petroleum Industry Act

quiz.q: Approximately how many barrels of oil per day does Nigeria lose to theft?
quiz.explanation: Nigeria is estimated to lose 400,000–600,000 barrels of oil per day to theft through illegal bunkering — tapping pipelines, using illegal refineries, and corrupt export schemes.

laws.title: Twitter/X Ban and Social Media Law
laws.subtitle: Nigeria banned Twitter in 2021 and has since sought to regulate social media
laws.fullDescription: In June 2021, Nigeria banned Twitter after the platform deleted a tweet by President Buhari referencing the civil war. The ban lasted 7 months — one of the longest social media bans in a democracy. Nigeria used its National Broadcasting Commission to enforce the ban on ISPs. Twitter unblocked after agreeing to open a local office, register as a company, pay taxes, and appoint a local representative. Nigeria's ongoing Nigerian Broadcasting Code applies to online streaming, and proposed social media bills (criticized by rights groups as censorship tools) have circulated. Nigeria's internet freedom has declined, with increasing use of network shutdowns during protests.
laws.penalty: Accessing banned platforms during the ban: NGN 200 ($0.40 at devalued rates) per connection (Airtel Nigeria charged subscribers); media companies violating NBC code: heavy fines
exceptions: VPN use to circumvent the ban was not prosecuted — used by millions during the ban

quiz.q: How long did Nigeria's Twitter ban last?
quiz.explanation: Nigeria banned Twitter from June 2021 to January 2022 — approximately 7 months — after Twitter deleted a tweet by President Buhari. It was one of the longest Twitter bans in a country with an elected government.

laws.title: EFCC Anti-Corruption Law
laws.subtitle: Nigeria's Economic and Financial Crimes Commission has prosecuted hundreds of officials
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria's Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) was established by the EFCC Act 2002 under US pressure as part of anti-money laundering compliance. The EFCC investigates and prosecutes financial crimes including advance fee fraud (419 fraud), money laundering, and public sector corruption. It has arraigned two former presidents (Obasanjo's PDP government officials), state governors, bank executives, and thousands of individuals. Nigeria is ranked among the world's most corrupt countries (Transparency International CPI: 145th of 180 in 2024). EFCC's effectiveness is debated — convictions are often delayed by prolonged court processes, and politically connected defendants have often avoided accountability.
laws.penalty: Money laundering: up to 14 years imprisonment; advance fee fraud (419): up to 20 years; public officer corruption: up to life imprisonment for some offenses
exceptions: Presidential immunity applies while officeholders are in power — prosecutions must wait until they leave office
State governors have been granted immunity by courts in some cases

quiz.q: What is '419 fraud' — a crime frequently prosecuted by Nigeria's EFCC?
options: Advance fee fraud (asking victims to pay upfront fees for promised large payoffs)
quiz.explanation: '419 fraud' is named after Section 419 of the Nigerian Penal Code that criminalizes advance fee fraud — the scheme where victims are promised large returns if they pay upfront fees. It's one of the world's most widely executed types of internet fraud.

laws.title: Same Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act 2014
laws.subtitle: Nigeria's federal law banning same-sex relationships carries 14 years imprisonment
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria's Same Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act, signed January 7, 2014 by President Goodluck Jonathan, is one of Africa's most comprehensive anti-LGBTQ+ laws. The Act: bans same-sex marriage and civil unions (up to 14 years imprisonment); criminalizes membership in organizations that support LGBTQ+ rights (up to 10 years); and prohibits public displays of same-sex affection (up to 10 years). Northern Nigeria under Sharia law has an additional penalty of stoning for homosexual acts. The law was met with strong international condemnation but popular domestic support — polls showed 98% of Nigerians opposed same-sex marriage. The law chilled LGBTQ+ rights advocacy and drove communities underground. Nigeria is Africa's most populous nation, making this law's impact particularly significant. The law also affects human rights organizations, journalists, and even medical professionals who work with LGBTQ+ communities.
laws.penalty: Same-sex marriage or civil union: 14 years imprisonment; supporting LGBTQ+ organizations: 10 years imprisonment; public same-sex affection: 10 years imprisonment; additionally, Sharia states have separate provisions including death penalty
exceptions: Medical treatment that incidentally involves LGBTQ+ individuals has no explicit exemption
Academic research is technically subject to the law if it 'supports' LGBTQ+ organizations
Diplomatic personnel in official capacity have immunity

laws.title: 'Japa' Brain Drain and Emigration Policies
laws.subtitle: Nigeria's mass emigration of professionals — known as 'Japa' — raises legal questions about human capital and rights
laws.fullDescription: 'Japa' (Yoruba for 'flee' or 'escape') became the defining phenomenon of Nigerian emigration in the 2020s, as hundreds of thousands of educated Nigerians — particularly doctors, nurses, engineers, and technology professionals — left for the UK, Canada, US, Australia, and other destinations. Between 2019 and 2023, an estimated 70,000 Nigerian doctors left for the UK alone. Nigeria has 95% fewer doctors per capita than the WHO recommends. The phenomenon created legal and policy debates: should Nigeria require public-funded medical professionals to work in Nigeria for a minimum period (bond scheme); should emigration be regulated; or should Nigeria create conditions that keep professionals home? The Nigerian constitution guarantees freedom of movement and does not permit forced labor, making mandatory service schemes legally complex. Nigeria's National Information Technology Development Agency has expanded tech visa programs with other countries. The CBN (Central Bank of Nigeria) has also addressed diaspora remittances ($20+ billion annually) as a critical formal financial flow.
laws.penalty: No criminal penalties for emigration; bond scheme violations by government-trained doctors: civil debt claims; unauthorized foreign currency transactions: CBN fines
exceptions: Healthcare workers going on approved international assignments have facilitated leave
Government scholarship holders have service agreements already in place
Freedom of movement is constitutionally protected — regulatory constraints must be proportionate

laws.title: Tinubu's Fuel Subsidy Removal and Naira Devaluation
laws.subtitle: Nigeria's new president removed the fuel subsidy and floated the naira, causing economic pain
laws.fullDescription: President Bola Tinubu, inaugurated in May 2023, immediately announced the removal of Nigeria's long-standing fuel subsidy — declaring 'subsidy is gone' in his inauguration speech. The subsidy had cost Nigeria billions annually while enriching a corrupt import cartel. Within months, the Central Bank of Nigeria also unified foreign exchange windows, causing the naira to lose over 70% of its value. Fuel prices quadrupled. Inflation hit 30%+, and millions fell into poverty. Despite the economic pain, the reforms were praised by the IMF and World Bank as necessary structural corrections. Tinubu faced massive protests ('EndBadGovernance') in August 2024 amid rising food insecurity.
laws.penalty: Fuel smuggling after subsidy removal: up to 21 years imprisonment under Petroleum Industry Act. Forex round-tripping: criminal prosecution under CAMA and CBN regulations.
exceptions: Mass transit and commercial farming operations eligible for some transition support
CNG (compressed natural gas) vehicles subsidized as alternative fuel measure

quiz.q: What did Bola Tinubu announce in his very first inaugural speech as Nigeria's president?
options: A new constitutional conference to reform Nigeria's federal structure
'Subsidy is gone' — ending Nigeria's expensive fuel subsidy
A 10-year infrastructure plan funded by China
Free education for all Nigerians up to university level
quiz.explanation: Tinubu's first words in policy terms were 'subsidy is gone' — immediately ending Nigeria's fuel subsidy in his inauguration speech, triggering quadrupling of fuel prices and enormous economic disruption.

laws.title: West Africa Coup Wave and Nigeria's ECOWAS Response
laws.subtitle: Military coups swept West Africa; Nigeria led failed efforts to restore democracy through ECOWAS
laws.fullDescription: Between 2021 and 2023, a wave of military coups swept West Africa: Mali (2021), Guinea (2021), Burkina Faso (2022, twice), and Niger (2023). Niger's July 2023 coup was particularly significant — it overthrew Mohamed Bazoum, a democratically elected president and key US counterterrorism partner, removing access to a major drone base. ECOWAS (Economic Community of West African States) threatened military intervention against Niger's junta, with Nigeria's Tinubu as ECOWAS chair leading these threats. The intervention never materialized. Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger formed the Alliance of Sahel States and withdrew from ECOWAS entirely, creating a major fracture in West African regional integration.
laws.penalty: Nigeria's participation in ECOWAS enforcement operations: under domestic armed forces law and ECOWAS authorization. Coup plotters: prosecuted under respective national laws.
exceptions: ECOWAS military intervention requires authorization by heads of state summit
Humanitarian corridors maintained even during ECOWAS sanctions on coup countries
laws.sourceLabel: Economic Community of West African States

quiz.q: What unprecedented step did Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger take in response to ECOWAS pressure after their coups?
options: They requested military intervention from Russia to defend against ECOWAS
They formed the Alliance of Sahel States and withdrew from ECOWAS entirely
They held early elections to appease ECOWAS demands
They expelled all French and American military bases simultaneously
quiz.explanation: Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger — all under military junta rule — formed the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) and withdrew from ECOWAS entirely, creating the biggest fracture in West African regional integration since ECOWAS's founding in 1975.

laws.title: Nigeria's Petroleum Industry Act
laws.subtitle: 2021 reform overhauled decades of oil sector regulation
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria's Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) 2021 completely overhauled the country's oil and gas sector after 20 years of failed reform attempts. The PIA commercialized the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC), converting it to NNPC Limited — a commercial entity. It established a 3% oil revenue contribution to host communities (the Host Community Fund), created the Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (MDPRA), and set new licensing frameworks. The PIA aims to attract investment to Nigeria's declining oil production while addressing host community grievances in the Niger Delta.
laws.penalty: Operating oil facilities without PIA license: criminal prosecution and facility seizure. Environmental violations: fines up to $2 million plus remediation costs. Host community fund non-payment: license suspension. Pipeline vandalism (by communities): 21 years imprisonment
exceptions: Existing licenses were converted to new PIA framework with transition provisions
Small-scale artisanal refining has a separate regulatory track
Gas flaring exemptions during transition period under approved flare-out programs

quiz.q: What percentage of oil revenue must go to host communities under Nigeria's Petroleum Industry Act?
quiz.explanation: Nigeria's Petroleum Industry Act 2021 requires oil companies to contribute 3% of their operating costs to a Host Community Development Fund for communities in oil-producing areas.

laws.title: Nigeria's Tinubu Fuel Subsidy Removal and CBN Reforms
laws.subtitle: 2023 shock reforms end decades of petrol subsidies and naira controls
laws.fullDescription: President Bola Tinubu's inauguration speech in May 2023 included the announcement 'subsidy is gone' — immediately ending Nigeria's petrol subsidy that had cost $10 billion annually. This caused petrol prices to triple overnight. Simultaneously, the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) unified the naira exchange rate, causing the naira to plummet 70%. These twin shocks caused significant inflation and economic hardship. Former CBN governor Godwin Emefiele was arrested on corruption charges. The reforms were praised by the IMF and World Bank as necessary but criticized for their social impact without adequate safety nets.
laws.penalty: Fuel subsidy fraud (under old system): up to 21 years under the Petroleum Industry Act. Foreign exchange manipulation: up to 10 years under BOFIA. Currency counterfeiting: up to 10 years. Profiteering during transition period: FCCPC enforcement action
exceptions: Fuel subsidies maintained for cooking gas (LPG) — social protection measure
Agricultural sector has subsidized inputs program maintained separately
Humanitarian organizations receive CBN approval for forex at preferential rates

quiz.q: What did President Tinubu announce in his inauguration speech regarding Nigeria's petrol subsidy?
options: 'Subsidy is gone' — immediately ending a $10 billion annual subsidy
He would maintain it for 5 more years
He would gradually phase it out over 10 years
quiz.explanation: In his inauguration speech on May 29, 2023, Tinubu declared 'subsidy is gone' — immediately ending Nigeria's petrol subsidy that had cost $10 billion annually and was enriching oil traders, causing petrol prices to triple overnight.

laws.title: Nigeria's Fintech Hub and Digital Finance Regulations
laws.subtitle: Africa's largest fintech ecosystem regulated by new frameworks
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria is Africa's largest fintech ecosystem — home to Paystack, Flutterwave, Opay, Kuda, and dozens of unicorns. The Central Bank of Nigeria enacted the revised Payment System Management Framework (2022), Regulatory Framework for Open Banking, and guidelines for Payment Service Banks (limited banking licenses for mobile money operators). The eNaira (central bank digital currency) was launched in 2021 — the first in Africa. Nigeria also launched a crypto regulatory framework under the SEC, reversing an earlier ban. The fintech ecosystem processes billions in transactions for the unbanked population.
laws.penalty: Operating unlicensed fintech business: CBN revocation and criminal prosecution. Money laundering through fintech platforms: up to 10 years under EFCC Act. Cryptocurrency fraud: prosecution under EFCC and Computer Crimes Act. eNaira fraud: prosecution under CBN Act
exceptions: Regulatory sandbox allows testing new financial products without full licensing
Diaspora remittance services have simplified compliance under IMTOs framework
Cooperative society lending is not regulated as banking

quiz.q: What was historically significant about Nigeria's eNaira launch in 2021?
options: It replaced the physical naira entirely
It was Africa's first central bank digital currency (CBDC)
It became the world's most traded digital currency
It enabled Nigeria to bypass US dollar transactions
quiz.explanation: Nigeria's eNaira, launched in October 2021, was Africa's first central bank digital currency (CBDC) — making Nigeria a global pioneer in state-issued digital currencies alongside China's e-CNY and The Bahamas' Sand Dollar.

laws.title: Cybercrime Act and Social Media Prosecution
laws.subtitle: Nigeria's Cybercrime Act criminalizes a wide range of online activities
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria's Cybercrimes (Prohibition, Prevention, etc.) Act 2015, amended in 2024, criminalizes cyberstalking, online fraud, identity theft, and sending messages 'likely to cause annoyance, inconvenience, danger, obstruction, insult, injury, criminal intimidation, enmity, hatred, ill will or needless anxiety.' Critics of the government have been prosecuted under the Act for social media posts. The 2024 amendment removed some contested provisions after civil society pushback but retained others. Nigeria also uses the Terrorism Prevention Act against critics labeled as security threats. Foreign nationals should be cautious about social media commentary on Nigerian politics.
laws.penalty: Sending offensive electronic messages: up to 3 years imprisonment or fine; cyberstalking: up to 3 years; financial fraud: up to 7 years
exceptions: Licensed journalists with press council credentials
Communications of religious organizations within approved frameworks

quiz.q: What broad standard in Nigeria's Cybercrime Act can lead to prosecution for online messages?
options: Messages likely to cause 'annoyance, inconvenience, or ill will'
quiz.explanation: Nigeria's Cybercrime Act includes prosecution for sending messages 'likely to cause annoyance, inconvenience, danger, obstruction, insult, injury, criminal intimidation, enmity, hatred, ill will or needless anxiety' — extremely broad language used against critics.

laws.title: Naira Redesign Crisis and Currency Control Laws
laws.subtitle: Nigeria's 2023 naira crisis created legal battles over cash access
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria's 2023 currency redesign policy — which replaced existing naira notes to fight corruption and inflation — created a catastrophic cash shortage when the Central Bank failed to distribute enough new notes before demonetizing old ones. Millions lost access to funds. The Supreme Court ordered the old notes to remain legal tender. President Buhari publicly defied the Supreme Court ruling — a major constitutional crisis. The Central Bank Governor was subsequently arrested for financial crimes. The episode highlighted tensions between the CBN's currency policies, banking law, and constitutional authority of courts. Nigerians faced fines for exchanging currency outside official channels during the crisis.
laws.penalty: Hoarding demonetized notes for unauthorized exchange: prosecution under currency regulations; defying CBN currency rules: criminal fines
exceptions: Businesses with documented transition difficulties given extension periods
Rural areas without banking infrastructure given additional time

quiz.q: What did Nigeria's Supreme Court order during the 2023 naira redesign crisis?
options: That all old notes be immediately destroyed
That old notes remain legal tender — which President Buhari publicly defied
quiz.explanation: Nigeria's Supreme Court ordered old naira notes to remain legal tender during the 2023 currency crisis, but President Buhari publicly defied the ruling — one of Africa's most dramatic confrontations between a president and the supreme court.

laws.title: Tinubu Government Subsidy Removal and Economic Reform Laws
laws.subtitle: Nigeria's Tinubu government removed fuel subsidies triggering economic turmoil
laws.fullDescription: President Bola Tinubu announced the removal of Nigeria's costly fuel subsidies on his inauguration day in May 2023 — saving the government an estimated $10 billion annually but immediately raising fuel prices 4-fold. The subsidy regime had been governed by the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) and NNPCL (Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited) regulations. Currency unification also dramatically devalued the naira. The combined economic shock triggered severe inflation and cost of living crisis. Legal challenges to specific implementation aspects were filed. The PIA created a new framework for oil sector governance, including compliance requirements for international oil companies.
laws.penalty: PIA regulatory violations: loss of operating licenses; currency manipulation after naira unification: criminal prosecution
exceptions: NNPCL as state entity has transition exemptions for certain legacy arrangements
Small-scale independent petroleum marketers received transitional support measures

quiz.q: When did Nigeria's Tinubu government announce fuel subsidy removal?
options: On his inauguration day in May 2023
quiz.explanation: President Tinubu announced Nigeria's fuel subsidy removal literally on his inauguration day in May 2023 — a shocking move that immediately quadrupled fuel prices and triggered severe inflation, though it eliminated a major drain on government finances.

laws.title: Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023
laws.subtitle: Nigeria enacts comprehensive data protection law
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria's Data Protection Act was signed into law in June 2023, establishing the Nigeria Data Protection Commission as the supervisory authority. The law grants data subjects rights to access, correction, and deletion of personal data, requires lawful basis for processing, mandates data protection impact assessments for high-risk activities, and introduces data breach notification within 72 hours. The law builds on the earlier Nigeria Data Protection Regulation (NDPR) and provides a stronger legal foundation.
laws.penalty: Fines up to 2% of annual gross revenue or 10 million naira (whichever is higher) for organizations; up to 2 million naira for individuals
exceptions: National security and law enforcement
Statistical and research purposes with appropriate safeguards
Journalistic activity serving public interest

quiz.q: What organization does Nigeria's 2023 Data Protection Act establish?
quiz.explanation: Nigeria's Data Protection Act 2023 established the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) as the dedicated supervisory authority for data privacy in the country.

laws.title: Nigeria Fuel Subsidy Removal and Economic Reform Laws
laws.subtitle: Nigeria removes costly petrol subsidies and floats the naira
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria's President Bola Tinubu dramatically removed the petrol subsidy on his inauguration day in May 2023, ending one of Africa's most expensive subsidies that had cost the government trillions of naira annually. The naira was also floated, leading to a sharp depreciation. These reforms, while economically necessary according to the IMF, caused immediate hardship with fuel prices quadrupling. Emergency social protection measures were enacted to cushion the impact on the poorest Nigerians.
laws.penalty: Fuel smuggling and illegal importation face enhanced criminal penalties; subsidy fraud from the previous regime being prosecuted
exceptions: Kerosene for cooking maintained as affordable energy for the poorest
Public transport operators received transitional support
Strategic fuel reserves managed under separate government rules

quiz.q: When did Nigeria's President Tinubu dramatically announce the removal of the petrol subsidy?
options: At a budget presentation six months after taking office
On his inauguration day in May 2023
quiz.explanation: President Tinubu announced the immediate removal of Nigeria's petrol subsidy on his inauguration day in May 2023, in one of the most dramatic first-day policy actions by a new Nigerian president.

laws.title: Nigeria Crypto and Binance Crackdown
laws.subtitle: Nigeria detains Binance executive and restricts crypto trading
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria detained a Binance executive in February 2024 and accused the company of facilitating capital flight and illegal financial operations. Nigeria demanded over $10 billion in fines from Binance, accusing it of enabling naira manipulation and moving billions in untaxed money. Nigeria also restricted access to crypto trading platforms. The actions reflected Nigerian authorities' frustration with the naira's sharp depreciation and allegations that crypto platforms were being used for currency speculation.
laws.penalty: Operating unlicensed crypto exchanges in Nigeria: criminal prosecution; currency manipulation: criminal prosecution; Binance facing: significant fines
exceptions: Crypto companies that register with the SEC and comply with CBN rules can operate
Blockchain research and development activities
Non-custodial wallets for personal use

quiz.q: What did Nigeria demand from Binance in 2024?
options: That Binance list the naira as a trading pair
Over $10 billion in fines and accused it of currency manipulation
That Binance register as a Nigerian bank
That Binance build local infrastructure in Nigeria
quiz.explanation: Nigeria demanded over $10 billion in fines from Binance in 2024, accusing the crypto exchange of facilitating currency manipulation, capital flight, and enabling billions in untaxed transactions during the naira's depreciation.

laws.title: Nigeria Data Protection Act
laws.subtitle: Nigeria's comprehensive personal data protection legislation
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria enacted the Nigeria Data Protection Act (NDPA), replacing the 2019 regulation with a proper legislative framework. The Act establishes the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) as an independent regulatory body, sets out rights for data subjects including access, correction, deletion, and portability, requires lawful bases for processing personal data, mandates data protection impact assessments for high-risk processing, and requires data controllers to appoint Data Protection Officers. Nigeria's large digital economy and fintech sector are significantly affected.
laws.penalty: Violations carry administrative fines of up to 2% of annual gross revenue or NGN 10 million, whichever is higher; intentional or negligent violations involving sensitive data carry higher penalties
exceptions: Processing for national security and law enforcement has modified requirements
Personal and household data processing exempt
Small data controllers have simplified obligations during initial compliance period

quiz.q: What body does Nigeria's Data Protection Act establish to regulate data privacy?
quiz.explanation: The Nigeria Data Protection Act establishes the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) as an independent regulatory authority responsible for enforcing data protection standards in Nigeria.

laws.title: Tinubu Economic Reforms
laws.subtitle: Nigeria's fuel subsidy removal and exchange rate unification
laws.fullDescription: President Bola Tinubu announced the immediate removal of Nigeria's petrol subsidy upon taking office in May 2023, ending a policy that had cost the government over USD 10 billion annually. Simultaneously, the Central Bank unified Nigeria's multiple foreign exchange windows into a single market-determined rate, causing the naira to depreciate sharply. These reforms, while painful in the short term with fuel prices tripling, were aimed at eliminating a major source of fiscal drain and currency distortion. Palliatives including cash transfers were promised but implementation was contested.
laws.penalty: Fuel price gouging above regulated levels carries fines and license revocation for petrol stations; illegal forex trading outside official channels carries fines and imprisonment
exceptions: Essential services like hospitals receive subsidized diesel for generators
Transportation operators received transition support
Remote communities in northern Nigeria have emergency supply arrangements

quiz.q: Approximately how much was Nigeria spending annually on petrol subsidies before President Tinubu removed them?
quiz.explanation: Nigeria was spending over USD 10 billion annually on petrol subsidies, which had become one of the largest fiscal burdens on the government, contributing to budget deficits and benefiting wealthy car owners more than the poor — the primary justification for the subsidy removal.

laws.title: Petroleum Industry Act Implementation
laws.subtitle: Nigeria's restructuring of its oil and gas sector
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria's Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) of 2021 began implementation, restructuring the entire oil and gas sector. The Act dissolved NNPC and replaced it with NNPC Limited (a commercial entity), created the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission and Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority, established a host community development fund, revised fiscal terms for oil production licenses, and created pathways for gas commercialization. Implementation has been uneven with some reforms moving forward and others facing industry resistance or funding challenges.
laws.penalty: Oil companies that fail to comply with new host community development obligations face fines; environmental violations in restructured regulatory framework carry enhanced penalties; fraud in license applications carries criminal liability
exceptions: Grandfathered existing licenses have transition provisions before fully adopting new fiscal terms
Small-scale local refineries have simplified licensing pathways
Marginal field operators have modified community development obligations

quiz.q: What replaced NNPC (Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation) under the Petroleum Industry Act?
options: NNPC Limited — a commercial entity rather than a government agency
The Nigerian Oil and Gas Authority
A private consortium of international oil companies
quiz.explanation: Nigeria's PIA replaced NNPC with NNPC Limited — transforming it from a government agency into a commercial entity that operates like a regular company, with the goal of improving efficiency, transparency, and profitability by separating commercial and regulatory functions.

laws.title: Nigeria Fuel Subsidy Removal and Naira Devaluation
laws.subtitle: Tinubu's shock economic reforms removing decades-long subsidies
laws.fullDescription: President Bola Tinubu announced the removal of Nigeria's costly petrol subsidy on his inauguration day (May 29, 2023), ending a decades-long program that cost the government over $10 billion annually. The subsidy removal caused petrol prices to triple immediately, triggering inflation exceeding 30%. Simultaneously, the Central Bank of Nigeria devalued and unified the naira exchange rate, causing the currency to lose over 70% of its value against the dollar. The reforms caused severe short-term economic hardship.
laws.penalty: Fuel smugglers exploiting post-subsidy price differentials with neighboring countries face imprisonment of 5–7 years under the Petroleum Industry Act 2021. Price gouging at filling stations carries fines and license revocation.
exceptions: Mass transit vehicles qualified for transitional transport support grants
Industries classified as strategic (power generation, food production) received partial transition subsidies for 6 months

quiz.q: On what occasion did President Tinubu announce the removal of Nigeria's fuel subsidy?
options: A national address one month after taking office
quiz.explanation: President Tinubu announced the removal of Nigeria's fuel subsidy on his very inauguration day, May 29, 2023, in a surprise policy declaration that immediately triggered a tripling of petrol prices and severe inflation.

laws.title: Nigeria Local Government Autonomy Supreme Court Ruling
laws.subtitle: Supreme Court grants financial independence to 774 local governments
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria's Supreme Court ruled in July 2024 that the 36 state governments could no longer withhold federal allocations meant for the 774 local government areas (LGAs), ordering direct payment of LGA funds from the federation account to local governments. Previously, state governors routinely diverted LGA funds. The ruling was seen as a landmark for fiscal federalism and local governance. Implementation required Central Bank cooperation and new remittance mechanisms, with some states initially resisting.
laws.penalty: State governors or officials who intercept or divert local government federal allocations following the Supreme Court ruling face criminal prosecution for stealing public funds, with sentences up to 14 years under Nigeria's Criminal Code.
exceptions: States may retain administrative roles in processing salary payments for LGA workers subject to verification
Emergency security situations in a state may allow temporary pooling of LGA and state resources under National Security Council protocols

quiz.q: How many local government areas in Nigeria were affected by the Supreme Court's July 2024 ruling on LGA autonomy?
quiz.explanation: Nigeria's July 2024 Supreme Court ruling directly affected all 774 local government areas (LGAs) in Nigeria, ordering that federal allocations be paid directly to LGAs rather than being channeled through (and often diverted by) the 36 state governments.

laws.title: Nigeria Non-Governmental Organizations Act Reform
laws.subtitle: Regulating civil society amid concerns about foreign funding
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria debated and advanced an NGO regulatory bill in 2023–2024 that would require all civil society organizations to register with a new government agency, disclose foreign funding sources, and obtain government approval for internationally-funded programs. Supporters argued it would prevent foreign influence; critics, including human rights organizations and Western donors, argued it would effectively silence civil society. Nigeria's history of government crackdowns on activists made the bill particularly controversial.
laws.penalty: NGOs that operate without registration under the proposed law: fines of NGN 1 million and potential forced closure. Organizations that receive foreign funds without disclosure: fines of NGN 5 million.
exceptions: Religious organizations already registered with the Corporate Affairs Commission subject to different regulatory framework
Academic research institutions not classified as NGOs for regulatory purposes
International organizations with UN Observer status or diplomatic accreditation subject to different framework

quiz.q: What was the main concern civil society organizations had about Nigeria's proposed NGO regulatory bill?
options: The registration fees were too high
It would effectively silence civil society through government approval requirements
It focused too much on large organizations
quiz.explanation: Civil society organizations and international donors feared Nigeria's NGO regulatory bill would effectively silence civil society by requiring government approval for internationally-funded programs — a concern heightened by Nigeria's history of government crackdowns on activists and journalists.

laws.title: Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) Implementation
laws.subtitle: Restructuring Nigeria's oil sector with new fiscal and governance rules
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria's Petroleum Industry Act — the most significant reform of the oil sector in decades — took effect, splitting NNPC into a commercial entity (NNPC Ltd), creating the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission, and restructuring royalties and taxes. It also established a 3% Frontier Exploration Fund and a Host Community Development Trust requiring oil companies to fund community projects.
laws.penalty: Companies failing to fund Host Community Trusts: suspension of operating licences; royalty underpayment: fines and back-payment with 15% interest
exceptions: Marginal field operators receive reduced fiscal burden during early production phases
Frontier exploration companies in deep offshore get tax holidays up to 10 years

quiz.q: What did Nigeria's Petroleum Industry Act transform NNPC into?
options: A commercial company (NNPC Ltd) with separate regulatory bodies
quiz.explanation: The PIA transformed NNPC into NNPC Limited — a fully commercial company — while creating separate regulatory bodies for upstream and midstream/downstream operations to improve governance.

laws.title: Naira Float and Forex Unification Reform
laws.subtitle: Nigeria ends currency peg, allows naira to find market rate
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria's new government under President Tinubu unified the multiple official and black market exchange rates into a single market rate, allowing the naira to float. The currency immediately depreciated over 40%. The IMF praised the reform as overdue, but the short-term impact included surging inflation, fuel price increases (after subsidy removal), and civil unrest. Foreign investment inflows began recovering.
laws.penalty: Unauthorised parallel forex trading: fines up to ₦50 million; banks violating CBN forex circulars: licence suspension risk
exceptions: Diplomatic missions continue to access forex at published rates
Export proceeds from pre-reform contracts can be repatriated under transitional rules

quiz.q: What happened to the naira immediately after Nigeria unified its exchange rates?
options: It was pegged to the dollar
quiz.explanation: After Nigeria unified its multiple exchange rates and allowed the naira to float freely, the currency immediately depreciated by over 40% against the dollar, reflecting years of overvaluation under the previous regime.

laws.title: Lagos Climate Adaptation and Flood Risk Management Law
laws.subtitle: Lagos State enacts coastal flooding and sea level rise protections
laws.fullDescription: Lagos State enacted a Climate Adaptation Strategy with legal backing, requiring coastal development setbacks, mandating flood risk assessments for all new construction in low-lying areas, and establishing a Lagos Climate Fund. The law responded to increasing flooding events and projections that parts of Lagos Island could be submerged by 2100. Slum upgrading programs in flood-prone Makoko area were also funded.
laws.penalty: Coastal construction within prohibited setback zones: demolition order; failure to conduct flood risk assessment: permit denial and fines
exceptions: Heritage structures in Victoria Island waterfront exempt from new setback rules under special review
Fishing communities receive community land use certificates with modified setback requirements

quiz.q: What is a primary long-term climate threat to parts of Lagos identified in its adaptation law?
options: Sea level rise that could submerge coastal areas by 2100
quiz.explanation: Sea level rise is identified as a primary long-term climate threat to Lagos, with projections suggesting that parts of Lagos Island could be submerged by 2100 — a key driver of the city's coastal adaptation legislation.

laws.title: Petroleum Industry Act Full Implementation
laws.subtitle: PIA reshaping oil sector governance
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria's Petroleum Industry Act 2021 reached full implementation phase in 2025-2026, restructuring NNPC into NNPC Limited, establishing the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission and the Midstream Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority. The law mandates host community development funds receiving 3% of operating expenditures, introduces competitive fiscal terms for deep offshore blocks, and requires gas flaring elimination by 2030. Non-compliance with host community provisions triggers operating license suspension.
laws.penalty: Operating license suspension; host community fund default incurs 0.05% of operating cost per day; gas flaring violations fined at $2 per thousand cubic feet flared
exceptions: Force majeure conditions for flaring
Transition periods for legacy infrastructure
Small-scale operations under 1,000 barrels/day may apply for extended timelines

quiz.q: Under the PIA, what percentage of operating expenditures must oil companies contribute to host community development funds?
quiz.explanation: The Petroleum Industry Act mandates 3% of operating expenditures go into host community development funds to benefit oil-producing communities.

laws.title: Nigeria Fintech Regulatory Framework and Digital Currency Expansion
laws.subtitle: Regulating Africa's largest fintech ecosystem
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria enacted the Fintech Governance and Digital Currency Act 2025, creating a comprehensive framework for Nigeria's fintech sector — the largest in Africa by investment and the home of unicorn companies like Flutterwave, Paystack, and Interswitch. The law creates the Nigeria Fintech Regulatory Authority as dedicated regulator (previously under CBN and SEC), establishes a regulatory sandbox with 18-month testing periods, mandates interoperability between all licensed payment systems, expands the eNaira (Nigeria's central bank digital currency) with programmable payment features for government transfers, introduces tiered KYC requirements enabling basic accounts with phone number only for unbanked population, and creates liability frameworks for AI-driven financial decisions.
laws.penalty: Operating unlicensed fintech service above 1 million transactions: ₦500 million fine; payment system non-interoperability: ₦200 million; eNaira fraud: 20 years imprisonment
exceptions: Agent banking networks in rural areas have 3-year extended compliance timeline
Informal savings groups (ajo/esusu) below ₦5 million exempt from full licensing
Cooperative societies have modified fintech framework under separate cooperative law

quiz.q: What is the name of Nigeria's central bank digital currency that the 2025 Act expands with programmable payment features?
quiz.explanation: Nigeria's eNaira is the central bank digital currency (CBDC) introduced in 2021, which the 2025 Fintech and Digital Currency Act expands with programmable payment features for government transfers and financial inclusion.

laws.title: Nigeria Tinubu Economic Reform and Subsidy Removal Legislation
laws.subtitle: Most ambitious Nigerian economic reform in decades
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria enacted the Economic Reform Consolidation and Social Protection Act 2025, codifying President Tinubu's shock therapy economic reforms. The law permanently eliminates petrol subsidies (which had cost $10 billion/year), establishes the Nigeria Social Investment Programme directing subsidy savings to targeted cash transfers for 15 million low-income households, creates the Nigerian Exchange Rate Unification Authority maintaining the floating naira regime, introduces a Natural Gas Monetization Programme converting stranded gas reserves to industrial feedstock and LNG, establishes the Nigerian Tax Code Modernization replacing the multiplicity of taxes with a simplified 5-tier system, and creates the Poverty Reduction and Economic Empowerment Fund with ₦5 trillion for microfinance and SME support.
laws.penalty: Subsidy fraud in successor fuel distribution: ₦1 billion plus 20 years imprisonment; exchange rate manipulation: ₦500 million plus banking license revocation; social transfer fraud: ₦100 million plus 15 years
exceptions: Kerosene subsidy for rural cooking maintained under modified support framework
Emergency fuel supply during natural disasters may use interim price controls
Agricultural sector fuel use (tractors) may have modified pricing during transition

quiz.q: Approximately how much per year had Nigeria's petrol subsidies cost before President Tinubu eliminated them?
quiz.explanation: Nigeria's petrol subsidies cost approximately $10 billion per year before President Tinubu's removal in 2023 — consuming a massive share of government revenues while disproportionately benefiting wealthier Nigerians who own vehicles and fuel distributors.

laws.title: Tinubu Fuel Subsidy Removal and Economic Reform Act
laws.subtitle: End of decades-long petrol subsidy and naira devaluation
laws.fullDescription: President Tinubu's government has enacted legislation formalizing the end of Nigeria's long-standing petrol subsidy regime and liberalizing the naira exchange rate. The reforms, while IMF-supported, caused immediate fuel price increases of over 300% and currency devaluation, triggering widespread hardship and protests. The law redirects subsidy savings to social investment programs including cash transfers and infrastructure, though implementation has been contested.
laws.penalty: Fuel smuggling across borders carries up to 14 years imprisonment and seizure of vehicles. Black market currency trading carries fines up to 10 times the traded amount.
exceptions: Emergency fuel allocations to hospitals and essential services are maintained at government-negotiated prices during transition
State governments receive direct cash transfers from subsidy savings to fund local social programs

quiz.q: By approximately how much did fuel prices increase when Nigeria ended its petrol subsidy under Tinubu?
quiz.explanation: Nigeria's fuel prices increased by over 300% when President Tinubu ended the decades-long petrol subsidy on his first day in office, causing widespread hardship and protests.

laws.title: Digital Economy and Fintech Regulation Act
laws.subtitle: Harnessing Nigeria's tech sector amid economic crisis
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria enacted comprehensive digital economy legislation to capitalize on its position as Africa's largest fintech hub, home to companies like Flutterwave and Paystack. The law creates a regulatory sandbox for fintech innovation, establishes data localization requirements, regulates cryptocurrency exchanges, creates licensing frameworks for mobile money operators, and expands digital payment acceptance requirements for government services.
laws.penalty: Unlicensed cryptocurrency exchanges operating in Nigeria face fines up to NGN 100 million and criminal prosecution of directors. Data localization violations carry fines up to 2% of annual global revenue.
exceptions: Startups under three years old and under NGN 100 million revenue operate under simplified sandbox rules
International remittance services have modified data localization requirements to enable cross-border payments

quiz.q: Which of these is a Nigerian fintech unicorn that processes payments across Africa?
quiz.explanation: Flutterwave, founded in Nigeria, became Africa's most valuable fintech startup and processes billions in payments across the continent, exemplifying Nigeria's position as Africa's leading fintech hub.

laws.title: Food Security Crisis and Agricultural Transformation Act
laws.subtitle: Addressing hunger amid economic crisis and insecurity
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria enacted food security legislation in response to severe food inflation following fuel subsidy removal and naira devaluation. The law creates emergency food import facilitation, establishes a national strategic food reserve, provides emergency agricultural inputs for small farmers, creates special courts for agricultural land disputes and bandit/farmer conflicts that had disrupted farming in the northwest, and expands irrigation infrastructure to reduce dependence on rainfall.
laws.penalty: Food hoarders who create artificial scarcity during declared food emergencies face up to 10 years imprisonment. Agricultural land grabbers who forcibly displace farmers face asset seizure and criminal prosecution.
exceptions: Small subsistence farmers are exempt from commercial agricultural compliance requirements
Traditional pastoral routes for herders that cross agricultural land retain customary protections with dispute resolution mechanisms

quiz.q: What two key Tinubu economic reforms dramatically increased food prices in Nigeria in 2023?
options: Fuel subsidy removal and naira devaluation
quiz.explanation: President Tinubu's removal of the petrol subsidy (increasing fuel prices over 300%) and floating of the naira (which lost 70% of its value) dramatically increased transportation and production costs, causing food inflation that severely hurt ordinary Nigerians.

laws.title: Lagos State Flood Management and Climate Adaptation Act
laws.subtitle: Africa's largest city adapting to sea level rise
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria enacted state legislation for Lagos — Africa's largest city and one of the world's fastest-growing megacities — creating a comprehensive climate adaptation program. The law mandates flood risk assessments for all new construction in Lagos, creates community flood early warning systems, funds drainage infrastructure upgrades, establishes building elevation requirements in flood-prone areas, creates managed retreat programs for communities in the most dangerous coastal zones, and prohibits new construction in high-risk areas.
laws.penalty: Developers who build in prohibited flood zones face demolition orders and up to 10 years imprisonment for responsible officials. Construction below mandatory elevation standards in flood-risk areas carries fines and structural compliance orders.
exceptions: Informal settlements in flood-risk areas receive relocation assistance rather than immediate demolition
Emergency reconstruction after flooding disasters receives expedited approvals with minimal delays

quiz.q: By how much is Lagos expected to grow in population by 2050?
options: It will decline as people leave
quiz.explanation: Lagos, already one of the world's largest cities with over 15 million people in the urban area, is projected to grow to 30-35 million or more by 2050 — potentially becoming the world's largest city — making flood management and climate adaptation urgent priorities.

laws.title: Nigeria Tinubu Economic Reform and Subsidy Removal Act
laws.subtitle: Fuel Subsidy Elimination and FX Reform Law
laws.fullDescription: Legislates President Tinubu's Day 1 economic shock therapy including petroleum subsidy removal and foreign exchange market unification. The law ends the NNPC fuel subsidy that cost $10 billion annually, unifies the multiple foreign exchange windows into a single market rate, establishes a cash transfer program for vulnerable Nigerians, creates the National Social Investment Programme expansion, and mandates oil sector transparency.
laws.penalty: Criminal prosecution for fuel subsidy fraud; fines for petroleum marketers violating deregulated pricing
exceptions: CNG and liquefied petroleum gas retain transitional support
Public transportation receives temporary fuel support during adjustment

quiz.q: How much did Nigeria's petroleum subsidy cost annually before Tinubu's removal?
quiz.explanation: Nigeria's petroleum subsidy cost approximately $10 billion annually before President Tinubu's Day 1 subsidy removal.

laws.title: Nigeria #EndBadGovernance Protest Response and Youth Inclusion Act
laws.subtitle: Democratic Accountability and Youth Political Rights Law
laws.fullDescription: Responds to the August 2024 #EndBadGovernance protests that echoed Kenya's Gen-Z movements, addressing demands for accountability, cost of living relief, and political inclusion. The law creates a National Youth Council with advisory powers, establishes mechanisms for youth representation in appointments, creates accountability for government spending commitments, mandates quarterly presidential addresses on economic conditions, and establishes community feedback mechanisms.
laws.penalty: Administrative accountability for officials failing to implement transparency commitments
exceptions: National security information excluded from transparency requirements
Personal data of government officials protected from public disclosure

quiz.q: What international youth movement inspired Nigeria's 2024 #EndBadGovernance protests?
quiz.explanation: Nigeria's 2024 #EndBadGovernance protests were inspired by Kenya's Gen-Z movement that had successfully forced withdrawal of Kenya's Finance Bill.

laws.title: Nigeria National Security and Terrorism Prevention Reform Act
laws.subtitle: Boko Haram and Bandits Counter-Terror Law
laws.fullDescription: Strengthens Nigeria's counter-terrorism framework addressing Boko Haram/ISWAP in the northeast and banditry in the northwest. The law creates the Terrorism Prevention and Prohibition Act revision, establishes the National Counter Terrorism Centre with expanded powers, creates community-oriented counter-radicalization programs, establishes legal frameworks for rehabilitated former fighters, and creates victims' reparation mechanisms.
laws.penalty: Death penalty for terrorism deaths; life imprisonment for terrorist acts; up to 40 years for financing
exceptions: Deradicalization program participants receive modified sentencing
Communities cooperating with counter-terrorism receive protection

quiz.q: What two security threats does Nigeria's Counter-Terrorism Act primarily address?
quiz.explanation: Nigeria's Counter-Terrorism Reform Act primarily addresses Boko Haram/ISWAP terrorism in the northeast and armed banditry in the northwest.

laws.title: Dangote Refinery Operations and Fuel Subsidy End
laws.subtitle: Africa's Largest Refinery Transforms Energy Sector
laws.fullDescription: The Dangote Petroleum Refinery in Lagos, Africa's largest refinery with 650,000 barrel per day capacity, reached substantial operations in 2024-25. Combined with President Tinubu's removal of fuel subsidies, Nigeria underwent a major energy sector transformation, with domestic refining reducing import dependence despite initial price shocks.
laws.penalty: No criminal penalties; market price adjustments affect consumers
exceptions: Phased implementation
Social intervention funds for vulnerable populations

quiz.q: What is significant about the Dangote Refinery?
options: It is Africa's largest oil refinery
quiz.explanation: The Dangote Petroleum Refinery is Africa's largest oil refinery with 650,000 barrels per day capacity, transforming Nigeria's fuel import dependence.

laws.title: Hunger Protests and Food Security Crisis
laws.subtitle: Nationwide Demonstrations Against Economic Hardship
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria experienced major hunger protests in August 2024 as citizens took to the streets over soaring food prices, fuel subsidy removal impacts, and naira devaluation. The government responded with a mix of security measures and social relief programs. The protests reflected deep frustrations with President Tinubu's economic reform agenda.
laws.penalty: Criminal penalties for violent protest; police response to demonstrations
exceptions: Constitutional right to peaceful assembly
Government social intervention programs

quiz.q: What triggered Nigeria's August 2024 hunger protests?
options: Soaring food prices, fuel subsidy removal, and currency devaluation
quiz.explanation: Nigeria's hunger protests were triggered by soaring food prices and economic hardship resulting from fuel subsidy removal and naira devaluation under Tinubu's reform agenda.

laws.title: Fintech Regulation and Digital Finance Leadership
laws.subtitle: Nigeria Leads Africa in Mobile Money and Fintech
laws.fullDescription: Nigeria emerged as Africa's leading fintech market with companies like Flutterwave, Paystack, and Opay processing billions in transactions. The Central Bank tightened fintech regulations including anti-money laundering requirements.
